title: synthetic-chaos-stress-profiles-2026
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

This page defines a set of synthetic stress profiles and a small chaos-harness used by SRE and Runtime teams to validate kernel scheduling, KV cache behavior, batching heuristics, and degradation/fallback policies under controlled but realistic failure modes. These profiles are used for:

- Pre-release performance gating (release branch + canary)
- Continuous nightly regression checks
- Capacity and autoscaling validation for Dedicated clusters
- On‑prem validation for Private deployments prior to customer handover

Goals

1. Provide reproducible workload definitions that exercise the hot paths across the serving runtime (attention kernels, kv-cache, batching, preemption).
2. Surface regressions in tail latency, correctness (token drift), and error modes introduced by kernel changes or scheduler refactors.
3. Validate fallback and graceful degradation policies (model variant fallback, region fallback).
4. Give a standardized triage playbook and pass/fail criteria tied to SLOs.

Scope and Exclusions

- Scope: inference path (token generation / chat), scheduler interactions, cache eviction under pressure, batching/packing, network backpressure.
- Exclusions: training workloads, model conversion artifacts, client-side SDK correctness.

Ownership

- Primary: eng-serving-runtime / Runtime QE (runtime-qe@redwood.com)
- Secondary: eng-sre (sre-runtime@redwood.com)
- Review cadence: Quarterly or on any scheduler/runtime release

Definition: Stress Profile Concept

Each stress profile is a small YAML spec interpreted by benchctl (internal harness). Required fields: id, description, tenant_mix, sequence_length_dist, qps_pattern, latency_target, duration, fault_injection. Optional: kernel_expectations.

Example profile (encoder-heavy burst):

---
# file: profiles/encoder-heavy-burst.yaml
id: encoder-heavy-burst
description: Short-lived burst of high-qps small-sequence encoder generation to stress kernel queueing and batching.
tenant_mix: ["plat_internal": 0.6, "external_vip": 0.4]
sequence_length_dist: {mean: 16, p95: 48}
qps_pattern: {type: burst, peak_qps: 4200, warmup: 10s, cooldown: 30s}
duration: 5m
latency_target: {p50_ms: 5, p95_ms: 18, p99_ms: 45}
fault_injection: {drop_gpu_cards: none, simulate_network_spike: 0}
kernel_expectations: ["kernel_queue_depth >= 128 at peak", "batcher_pack_rate >= 90%"]
---

In the harness this becomes a single benchctl run:

$ benchctl run --profile profiles/encoder-heavy-burst.yaml --target cluster://staging-gpu-pool --output results/encoder-burst-2026-03-01.json

Key Stress Profiles (canonical list)

- kvcache-eviction-surge: simulate many long-context requests causing KV-cache churn and eviction storms. Useful to surface cache-serialization/lock contention.
- longcontext-steady: continuous long sequence generation (avg 4096 tokens) to exercise backend memory pressure and attention kernel breakpoints.
- mixed-tenant-thundering-herd: many small tenants with spiky arrivals to validate priority accounting and kernel-credit throttling.
- encoder-heavy-burst: short, high qps encoder-style workloads that produce large batching opportunities but stress kernel queueing (example above).
- ablate-batcher: toggle batcher parameters (max_latency_ms, max_tokens) across runs to measure cost/latency tradeoffs.
- graceful-degrade-path: incrementally reduce preferred model capacity and validate automatic fallback to lower-cost quantized variants without correctness regressions.

Pass/Fail Criteria and SLOs

Pass conditions are evaluated per-run and are used by CI gating and nightly regression alerts. Each profile tie to an action level:

- Green: all SLOs met and no increase in token-error or hallucination metrics beyond historical baseline
- Amber: specific SLO breach but within tolerable rollback policy (e.g., p99 up to 1.5x baseline) -> alert + triage
- Red: major degradation (p99 > 2x or error_rate > 0.2%) -> block merge and trigger incident process

Default SLO thresholds (adjust per workload):

- p50 latency <= profile.latency_target.p50_ms
- p95 latency <= profile.latency_target.p95_ms
- p99 latency <= profile.latency_target.p99_ms
- request_error_rate <= 0.1%
- token_drift (from golden prompts) <= 1% relative token mismatch

Telemetry and Metrics to Collect

Collect these during every run:

- infra: GPU utilization per-card, memory_used, PCIe retransmits, host-side CPU stall time
- runtime: per-kernel exec_time histogram, kernel_queue_depth, batch_size_distribution, batch_pack_rate, kvcache_eviction_rate, kvcache_lock_wait_ms
- api-level: request_latency histogram, error_codes, response_token_counts, token_drift_against_golden
- orchestration: container_restart_count, preemptions, model_variant_fallbacks

Suggested Prometheus metrics and dashboards (names):

- runtime_kernel_latency_ms_bucket{kernel}
- runtime_kernel_queue_depth_gauge
- runtime_batch_pack_ratio
- runtime_kvcache_evictions_total

Profiling Playbook (when a run fails)

1. Identify failing profile and time window. Pull benchctl artifact JSON and stored logs.
2. Check orchestration events (kube events, preemptions). If containers restarted or OOMKilled, escalate to eng-infra.
3. Correlate p99 spikes with kernel_latency histograms. If a single kernel shows a long tail, tag suspect kernel.
4. Enable sampling profiler run (trace-level) for 60s on the affected node group:

$ benchctl profile --node-group staging-gpu-pool --sample-duration 60s --output traces/trace-$(date +%s).json

5. If kvcache_eviction_rate > 10/min during failure, run the cache inspection script to dump kvcache shards and eviction logs:

$ benchctl kvcache-dump --node node-12 --shard 3 --out kvdump.json

6. If batch_pack_ratio drops below expected threshold, validate the request packing logs and the per-tenant sequence_length_dist used by the harness.

Runbook: Immediate Mitigations During Incidents

- Scaling: Temporarily scale Dedicated pool by +20% capacity (if autoscaling not reacting)
- Routing: Route high-priority tenants to a warm reserve pool (route policy: limit concurrency to 50% of default)
- Kernel gate: If a new kernel change is suspected, rollback kernel binary on canaries via the artifact manager and re-run the failing profile.
- Fallback: Toggle model_variant_fallback to allowed for the route to shift traffic to quantized variant.

Example commands (ops):

$ rctl cluster scale staging-gpu-pool --delta 10
$ rctl route update --route high-priority --capacity 50%
$ rctl artifact rollback --service runtime-kernel --to-revision v2026-02-22

Integration with Release Process

- New runtime/kernel code: required to run the full canonical profile set as part of pre-merge CI. Any Red/Amber outcome must be explained in a pre-merge checklist.
- Canary: deploy to a canary cluster and run only the high-sensitivity profiles (kvcache-eviction-surge, longcontext-steady).
- Automated gating: CI jobs will annotate PRs with benchctl artifacts and link to the profile run result.

Known Issues and Workarounds (as of 2026-03-01)

- Issue: kernel_credit accounting may under-report when mixed-tenant-thundering-herd runs with priority inversion.
  Workaround: temporarily increase per-tenant minimum credits and re-run the profile.
- Issue: Rare token drift observed for graceful-degrade-path when fallback quantized models differ in BOS tokenization.
  Workaround: add normalization step comparing token ids and run token-drift acceptance test in harness.
- Issue: benchctl sampling profiler may miss short-lived micro spikes due to 1s sampling resolution.
  Workaround: increase sample-duration to 120s or enable high-res tracer in suspected runs.

Gallery: Example results snippet (benchctl output)

{
  "profile_id": "kvcache-eviction-surge",
  "p99_ms": "132",
  "error_rate": "0.03%",
  "kvcache_evictions_per_min": "16",
  "kernel_outliers": ["attention_forward_v3", "kv_sync"]
}

Regression Triage Template

1. Summary: short description of observed failure and impacted SLOs.
2. Artifacts: benchctl run JSON, traces, node metrics, orchestration events.
3. Hypothesis: one-liner suspected cause.
4. Action taken: rollback/scale/toggle fallback, and result.
5. Root cause analysis: completed within 72 hours for red-level regressions.
6. Postmortem and mitigations: documented and assigned.

Automation and CI Examples

- GitHub Action snippet to run the canonical profiles on every kernel PR:

name: runtime-benchmark-check
on: pull_request
jobs:
  bench:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Run benchctl canonical set
        run: |
          benchctl run-set --set canonical --target cluster://ci-gpu-small --out artifacts/${{ github.sha }}.json || exit 1

Next Steps and Roadmap

- Expand the canonical set with a dedicated latency-sensitivity profile for each new kernel (ETA Q2 2026).
- Add synthetic network partition scenarios to the harness (ETA Q3 2026).
- Integrate benchctl outputs into the Runtime Console for per-PR visual diffs (ETA Q3 2026).

Appendix: Benchctl workload spec quick reference

Fields (string): id, description, duration, target_cluster
Fields (numeric): peak_qps, mean_sequence_length, p95_sequence_length
Fields (enums): qps_pattern (steady|burst|sine), fault_injection (none|network_spike|card_drop), validation (none|golden_token_set)
